correctness.rationale: A rook graph has diameter at most two. Under its line graph identification, the three distinct cells of a forbidden geodesic are exactly three selected edges forming a simple three-edge path in K_{m,n}; the fourth rectangle edge may be present. In each connected path-free bipartite component a spanning tree must be a star, and no extra edge can join two leaves in the same bipartition class. Conversely, stars have no such path. The labeled component series has isolated rows and columns, one type for a single edge, and one center choice for each higher-degree star. Summing gives ue^{vz}+ve^{uz}−uvz, and taking a set gives the stated exponential; differentiating by u gives the recurrence, including the empty-board bases. A forest has number of edges equal to occupied vertices minus nontrivial components. When both sides are at least three equality at m+n−2 needs two spanning components with opposite-side centers; selecting these centers specifies all edges, yielding mn. With m=2<n, a degree-two column would use both rows and isolate that star, leaving at most two edges; at the maximum n each column therefore chooses one of two rows, yielding 2^n. The 2×2 and one-row cases are immediate from the cycle and complete graph. An independently written finite check at /workspace/audit_evidence/replay.py (rook) compared metric-triple enumeration with the exact truncated component product on 28 boards and 78,035 subsets. The frozen 50 small boards are included in, not disjoint from, the 484 positive-side size pairs with extremal checks; this is only a wording issue in the verification summary.

evidence: Anand et al. characterize general-position sets by induced clique components and intercomponent distances. On rook graphs the diameter-two condition makes distinct induced clique components distance two, giving the structural characterization but not an enumerative formula.

Iršič et al. count Cartesian products of paths rather than the full complete-factor family. The general labeled bipartite-graph paper discusses the exponential formula without the required star restriction. The scalar degree m+n−2 is credited as established in prior Cartesian-product work.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These contributions supply the invariant and structural and enumerative methods or the maximum only. The strongest overlap is the direct rectangular rook-graph result in the catalogue, not the path-grid or generic labeled-graph results.
